title: Only 7% Pass This Cambridge Entrance Exam
summary: Patterns, scientific evidence, data and hidden mechanisms test how tightly you can control every variable.

landing.intro:
10 questions. Evidence, patterns and logic.
Can you spot what others miss?

about.body:
This worldwide entertainment challenge contains ten Cambridge-inspired questions across numerical patterns, experiments, scientific reasoning, data interpretation and spatial thinking. The final questions combine rules rather than testing obscure facts.

Choose the best answer using the information shown and basic maths and science knowledge. Your score appears after the final reveal. You can then unlock a review of the questions you answered incorrectly and their correct answers.

This is not an official University of Cambridge admissions test, application assessment or prediction of admission.

steps: Complete ten carefully selected questions in one focused challenge.
Choose one answer per question. Your score stays hidden until the final reveal.
Reveal your result, then unlock the breakdown and correct answers to the questions you missed.

about.disclaimer: Independent entertainment challenge. Not an official Cambridge admissions test and not affiliated with any university.

stage-1.preAdCopy: Your quiz score and results across three skill areas are ready to reveal.

profile-1.title: The Systems Standout
profile-1.copy: You answered nine or ten questions correctly—a strong result in this challenge. It reflects these ten questions, not your chances of university admission.

profile-2.title: The Cambridge Natural
profile-2.copy: You answered eight of ten questions correctly and reached the 80% target. Unlock the review to see the correct answers to the two questions you missed.

profile-3.title: The Analytical Thinker
profile-3.copy: You answered seven questions correctly. One more correct answer would have reached the 80% target. The optional review shows the correct answers to the questions you missed.

profile-4.title: The Methodical Thinker
profile-4.copy: You answered six questions correctly. Two more correct answers would have reached 80%. You can unlock the review to revisit the questions you missed.

profile-5.title: The Promising Problem-Solver
profile-5.copy: You answered five of ten questions correctly. Unlock the review to revisit the questions you missed and see their correct answers.

profile-6.title: The Curious Investigator
profile-6.copy: You answered fewer than five questions correctly. If you want to explore the questions further, unlock the review to see the correct answers to the ones you missed.

cambridge-s1q6.question: Two otherwise identical plants receive different fertilisers. Which growing conditions should stay the same to make a fair comparison?

cambridge-s2q8.question: Which variable is measured as the outcome of an experiment?

cambridge-s2q7.question: A beaker reading rises from 40 mL to 55 mL after an object is submerged. What volume is displaced?

cambridge-s3q3.question: Starting at 3, repeat this full rule to get each next term: add 2, then multiply by 2. Which sequence is correct?

cambridge-s3q8.question: A claim predicts X. The experiment observes not-X under valid conditions. What is the best response?

cambridge-s4q7.question: Which description shows reflection rather than rotation?

answers.a1: A left-facing shape flipped to face right across a vertical line

cambridge-s5q8.question: A model predicts 12, 18 and 24 for three trials. Actual values are 13, 17 and 24. What is the total absolute error?

cambridge-s5q5.question: A marker moves 2 units north, 3 units east, then 2 units south. Where is it relative to the starting point?

cambridge-s5q7.question: A sensor always reads 2 units above the true value. It currently shows 26. The true value falls by 5. What will the sensor show next?
